title: A Machine Learning Approach for Predicting 30-Day Hospital Readmission in Patients with Diabetes
relevance: Same dataset (Diabetes 130); shows the calibration and decision-curve work we still owe
summary: Predicts 30-day readmission on the 101,766-row Diabetes 130 data with logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and a stacking ensemble. Uses nested cross-validation, Platt calibration, 1,000 bootstrap resamples, decision-curve analysis and SHAP. Best stacking model: nested-CV ROC-AUC 0.664 (0.688 after calibration), Brier score 0.094. Same ceiling as ours.

title: Explainability in Forecasting Hospital Readmissions with Machine Learning
relevance: Same dataset; a published example of the accuracy trap
summary: Diabetes 130 data after deduplication (8.6% readmitted). Ensemble models reached 91.4% accuracy (LightGBM) but low recall because of the imbalance. SHAP and LIME point to length of stay, age, discharge disposition and A1C/glucose as main drivers, which matches our SHAP findings.

title: Detecting and Mitigating AI Bias in Health Care: Development and Validation of a Unified Multistage Framework
relevance: Same dataset; bias-audit framework we could borrow for our fairness section
summary: Audits Diabetes 130 (patient-level 80/20 split) and a Medicare synthetic file for representation, missingness, proxy, integrity and temporal bias. Mitigations (missingness features, weights; race excluded from prediction and used only for auditing) show a fairness-calibration-discrimination trade-off, not a uniform improvement, and do not establish deployment readiness.

title: Predicting 30-Day Hospital Readmission in Patients With Diabetes Using Machine Learning on Electronic Health Record Data
relevance: Closest published benchmark (already in our repo)
summary: Cureus 2025: logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost and a deep network on the UCI data. AUROC 0.642, 0.630, 0.667, 0.579. Reported accuracy about 0.89 equals the always-'no' baseline; the readmitted-class recall in its own Table 2 is only 0.2% to 14%. Cite AUROC only.

title: Fair and robust early readmission risk prediction from electronic health records via diffusion-based data augmentation and causal-invariant representation learning
relevance: Fairness and cross-race generalisation for diabetes readmission; uses synthetic augmentation, unlike us
summary: Proposes a diffusion-based fairness augmentation plus causal-invariant domain generalisation for early readmission in diabetes across racial groups. Reports roughly +2.0 points AUC and +1.5 points accuracy and over 25% lower demographic-parity and equalised-odds gaps. Check the dataset and whether augmentation is confined to training data (full text).

title: Predicting and Validating 30-day Hospital Readmission in Adults With Diabetes Whose Index Admission Is Diabetes-related
journal: The Journal of clinical endocrinology and metabolism
relevance: Parsimonious clinical model with an external-validation design
summary: Predicts 30-day readmission in 2,355 adults with diabetes whose admission was diabetes-related (11% readmitted). Four predictors (length of stay, ischaemic heart disease, peripheral vascular disease, number of drugs) give c-statistic 0.68, 0.67 cross-validated and 0.64-0.68 in three simulated external datasets.

title: Prediction of 30-day readmission in diabetes management using Machine learning
relevance: Small clinic dataset; not comparable to ours, useful as a caution
summary: Diabetes clinic in India, only 352 records. XGBoost best on precision 0.84, recall 0.87 and F1 0.85; random forest has AUC-ROC 0.94. The authors note random forest suits small datasets. The tiny sample and high scores need scrutiny before any comparison (abstract only; full text not open).

title: Deep Learning vs Traditional Models for Predicting Hospital Readmission among Patients with Diabetes
journal: AMIA ... Annual Symposium proceedings. AMIA Symposium
relevance: Shows history and labs lift performance, which our data lacks
summary: In 2,836,569 encounters of 36,641 diabetes patients, a deep LSTM model beat the best traditional model (AUC 0.79 vs 0.72 for random forest). Performance grew with prior encounters up to 30, and 16 selected lab tests matched all 981. This is the Temple paper we could not reach earlier.

title: Hospital Readmissions for Fluid Overload among Individuals with Diabetes and Diabetic Kidney Disease: Risk Factors and Multivariable Prediction Models
relevance: Adds psychosocial predictors, which our data lacks
summary: Risk models for readmission for fluid overload in people with diabetes and diabetic kidney disease. Adding clinical and psychosocial predictors improved risk reclassification (net reclassification improvement), supporting a transitional-care focus.

title: Evaluating Algorithmic Bias in 30-Day Hospital Readmission Models: Retrospective Analysis
relevance: Fairness metrics applied to LACE and HOSPITAL; good template for our subgroup analysis
summary: 10.6 million discharges from Maryland and Florida (2016-2019). LACE, the modified HOSPITAL score and a CMS readmission measure were applied as-is and retrained, then checked for bias between Black and White patients and between income groups using false-negative and false-positive rate parity. Fairness metrics flag disparities but cannot explain their causes.

title: Identifying and mitigating algorithmic bias in the safety net
relevance: Practical bias mitigation for a readmission model
summary: A safety-net health system found its unplanned-readmission model was most biased by insurance. Threshold adjustment by subgroup met the success criteria (equal-opportunity gap under 5 points, accuracy loss under 10%, alert rate change under 20%); reject-option classification did not. Includes a low-resource playbook.

title: Effective hospital readmission prediction models using machine-learned features
relevance: LACE comparison with machine-learned features
summary: 428,669 patients in Alberta (5.83% readmitted within 30 days). A gradient-boosting model on machine-learned plus manual features beat both a manual-feature model and the LACE model on AUC.

title: Comparison of LACE and HOSPITAL Readmission Risk Scores for CMS Target and Nontarget Conditions
journal: American journal of medical quality : the official journal of the American College of Medical Quality
relevance: Clinical-score benchmark: LACE vs HOSPITAL
summary: 291,886 encounters from two academic centres. LACE slightly outperformed HOSPITAL overall (AUROC 0.73 vs 0.69) but HOSPITAL did better for four CMS target diagnoses, lung cancer and colon cancer.

title: Predicting readmission to the cardiovascular intensive care unit using recurrent neural networks
relevance: Deep-learning readmission model on PhysioNet data (read for methods only)
summary: LSTM on MIMIC-III time series to decide whether a cardiovascular ICU patient can be discharged safely. Compared with logistic regression, random forest, extra trees, a feed-forward network and another LSTM, mainly on area under the precision-recall curve.

title: Hospital Re-Admission Prediction Using Named Entity Recognition and Explainable Machine Learning
relevance: Text-based readmission prediction
summary: Uses MIMIC-III discharge notes: a pretrained biomedical named-entity model extracts features, then machine-learning models predict unplanned readmission. Reports average precision 88.4% with gradient boosting and adds explainable AI. Check how the data were balanced.

title: Prediction of unplanned 30-day readmission for ICU patients with heart failure
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
relevance: Process mining plus a neural network for ICU heart-failure readmission
summary: Predicts unplanned 30-day readmission of ICU patients with heart failure from event logs (Decay Replay Mining) combined with demographics and severity scores. Reports accuracy 0.841 and F-score 0.800, better than its baselines. ICU population, not ours.

title: Knowledge Graph Embeddings for ICU readmission prediction
journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
relevance: Knowledge-graph features for readmission
summary: Enriches EHR data with ontology annotations to build a knowledge graph and learns embeddings for ICU readmission prediction, arguing that scientific context improves clinical machine learning.

title: HR-BGCN : Predicting readmission for heart failure from electronic health records
relevance: Check for the same oversampling-leakage risk as EmbPred30
summary: Heart-failure patients from MIMIC-III split into no readmission, readmission within 30 days and after 30 days. A graph model (HR-BGCN) with an Adaptive-TMix augmentation for minority classes reports 88.26% F1 and 90.47% accuracy. Look carefully at where the augmentation sits relative to the evaluation split.

title: Explainable Machine-Learning Model for Prediction of In-Hospital Mortality in Septic Patients Requiring Intensive Care Unit Readmission
relevance: Low relevance: predicts in-hospital death, not readmission
summary: MIMIC-IV v1.0 septic patients who were readmitted to the ICU; nine ML models predict in-hospital mortality, with an explainable model on the best performer.
